short: Zero-shot cross-corpus AVSR testing (M12) and a video-call test set (M11) are standard after WildVSR; each condition mixes several shifts, without repeated runs.
position: The paper [@jain2026] changes the evaluation (M12), testing three released AVSR checkpoints zero-shot in three input modes on six datasets, and the reference (M11), an Easy/Hard RoomReader video-call set. Both are standard: testing publicly released checkpoints outside LRS3 was already done in WildVSR [@djilali2023wildvsr], and concurrent work tests the same checkpoints on conversational video [@kwak2026voxmm] and on an LRS3-matched unseen set over five runs [@lin2026mv2lrs3], which shares the target's senior author. The main claim, that broadcast WER overstates generalization, holds, but each condition shifts speaking style, vocabulary, transmission, pose and preprocessing at once, and the design does not separate them. Auto-AVSR visual-only WER on RoomReader-AV exceeds 100% even on Easy clips (Table X), so the collapse lies mainly in the video channel, not only in short turns; Hard clips add 21.6 points (inference). The authors' blame on the LLM decoder for the Llama-AVSR failure (§IV-E, §V) rests on one run per condition, without variance.
